source.title: *-CFQ: Analyzing the Scalability of Machine Learning on a Compositional Task
source.authors: Dmitry Tsarkov; Tibor Tihon; Nathan Scales; Nikola Momchev; Danila Sinopalnikov; Nathanael Schärli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how error-rate curves change with training-set size in a compositional semantic-parsing task, using a different task and measure from language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own Transformer error-rate results as training examples, rule scope, compound divergence, and training-data mixture vary. These results bear on V7's curve-shape/setup-dependence aspect. It does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss, vary parameter count or training compute as scaling variables, fit small-run laws to predict larger runs, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The cited language-model scaling results are background, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own error-rate-versus-training-set-size curves for a fixed-size Transformer trained with supervised learning on semantic parsing. This is a new training regime, so it bears on whether a power-law data-scaling form holds beyond LM pretraining (V5). It does not measure LM pretraining loss or vary parameters or compute, and it fits no exponents. V1–V4, V6 and V7 are therefore not tested. The reader's V7 link is wrong: V7 concerns how fitted exponents and compute-optimal splits depend on setup and fitting choices. Here the bending comes from a deliberately fixed model and compute bottleneck, which the authors name as the cause.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In addition, the authors state that error rates keep falling with data at high compound divergence where random-split error has already plateaued. They attribute the plateaus mainly to the fixed model size and training steps, not to a failure of power-law scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed-size, fixed-training-step Transformer for semantic parsing and measures task error rate against training examples, rule scope, and compound divergence; it does not measure language-model pretraining cross-entropy or sweep parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Curve levels and flattening vary with rule scope, compound divergence, related-domain distance, target-to-supplementary data balance, and whether target examples are upweighted.
record.problems: The tested task is generated semantic parsing, not language-model pretraining. Model size and training steps are held fixed, so the study cannot assess parameter/token/compute scaling or compute-optimal allocation. Many curve values in the main figures are presented graphically; the compound-divergence table reports error rates with confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Omitted separate figure results include Figure 4(a) (the 10k target-data upweighting condition), Appendix I Figures 10–11 (additional target-data sizes and related-domain choices), Appendix J Figures 12–13 (N-CFQ and half-N-CFQ mixtures), and Appendix B Figures 5–6 (grounded/ungrounded comparisons). These are not included because the table entries for all reported compound-divergence and training-size combinations were retained first, followed by the main rule-scope and related-domain curve conditions.

untested.parts: LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; no LM pretraining is done.
No fits on small runs used to predict larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation; model size and steps are fixed.
No shape variation at fixed parameters.
Model-size and compute scaling in this regime; no fitted exponents or functional form; other modalities.
No relation of downstream performance to model scale or pretraining loss.
No exponents fitted or compared, and no fitting-method or parameter-counting variation.

missing.what: Error rate vs number of training steps (35k to beyond 500k): consistent gains with diminishing returns after 500k, larger at large training sizes.
Plateau values for equal-weighted mixtures (half-L ~0.03, L ~0.02, half-X ~0.04, X ~0.03); no gain from related data once target data reaches 200k.
Grounded vs ungrounded data-scaling curves from 9.5k to 8.7M examples follow qualitatively similar trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. The model is tiny (2 layers, hidden size 128) and model size is held fixed by design. The plateaus therefore reflect the model-size bottleneck that V1 itself excludes, and should not be read as challenging the power-law claims. Table 9 rows are individual points; their verdict-relevant content is the curve shape across sizes.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss and power-law scaling in language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
Fitting power laws on small runs and predicting much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Comparisons of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling in other modalities or training regimes such as image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.
Downstream performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss; this paper varies semantic-parsing training-set size instead.

Does not fit exponents, compare published exponents, vary parameter-counting or fitting methods, or test compute-optimal allocation. Results concern error-rate curves for one fixed-size Transformer on a compositional task.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: not stated; hidden size 128, 2 layers, 16 heads
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated error rate across training-set sizes on U-CFQ compound-divergence splits.
rows.note: One training-size/divergence entry; the paper describes rough power-law behavior over some ranges and flattening at large sizes.
rows.check: Relink from V7 to V5. Single table points cannot show a power law alone; read together, CD 0.0 error falls 0.014→0.004 by 61,879 examples, then flat at 0.005 to 1M (plateau under fixed model size).

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: not stated; hidden size 128, 2 layers, 16 heads
rows.operation_detail: Measured error-rate curves as training-set size increased across the rule-set lattice.

conditions.value: B-CFQ, half-N-CFQ, N-CFQ, half-L-CFQ, L-CFQ, half-X-CFQ, X-CFQ
fixed model size and fixed training steps

rows.value: Initially rough power-law variation for all rule scopes, then flattening at larger training sizes; X-CFQ plateaus at roughly 3 times the error rate of B-CFQ.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 1 averages 5 replicas; error bars are 0.95 confidence-level error margins.
rows.note: Text describes the curve and the approximate plateau comparison; individual plotted point values are not stated.
rows.check: Relink to V5. Rough power law initially for all rule scopes, then plateau at ~100–300k under fixed model and steps; X-CFQ plateau ~3x B-CFQ.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: not stated; hidden size 128, 2 layers, 16 heads
rows.operation_detail: Varied supplementary related-domain training examples while holding target-domain training data at 10k examples.
rows.measure: Error rate versus total training-set size
rows.baseline: 10k target-domain examples; no single baseline value stated
rows.value: The curve initially follows a clear power-law relation up to around 100k–300k examples, depending on dataset, then plateaus; greater domain distance gives slower error reduction and a higher plateau.
rows.uncertainty: 5 replicas per split; no numeric uncertainty stated for this result.
rows.note: Outcome described in the text across supplementary-domain choices; no per-domain numeric values are stated here.
rows.check: Relink to V5. 'Clear power law' up to ~100–300k total examples, then plateau; slower decline and higher plateau for more distant domains.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: not stated; hidden size 128, 2 layers, 16 heads
rows.operation_detail: Varied supplementary related-domain training examples while holding target-domain training data at 100k examples.
rows.measure: Error rate versus total training-set size
rows.baseline: 100k target-domain examples; no single baseline value stated
rows.value: Benefit from supplementary data is more limited; error rates increase when supplementary data substantially exceeds target-domain data. Near a 100x supplementary-to-target ratio, errors are comparable to the plateaus in Figure 3(a) for the same related-domain choice.
rows.uncertainty: 5 replicas per split; no numeric uncertainty stated for this result.
rows.note: Outcome described in the text; individual plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Relink to V5. With 100k target examples, error increases as off-distribution supplementary data grows well beyond target data. The added data are from a shifted distribution, so this is a data-mixture effect, not pure scaling.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.size_stated: not stated; hidden size 128, 2 layers, 16 heads
rows.operation_detail: Varied supplementary related-domain training examples while retaining at least half of training observations as target-domain examples.

conditions.value: target examples upweighted to maintain at least half of observations

rows.value: Added related-domain examples can yield positive effects in most cases, but more distant domains drop more slowly and reach higher plateaus.
rows.uncertainty: 5 replicas per split; no numeric uncertainty stated for this result.
rows.note: Text gives the qualitative curve outcome; individual plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Relink to V5. Upweighted target data gives mostly positive effects, but slower declines and higher plateaus for distant domains.

relationships.condition: Random splits and low-divergence supervised semantic parsing, moderate training sizes (~10k to ~100–300k examples)
relationships.reason: Authors report error falling in a rough or 'clear' power law with training size before the fixed-model plateau (C57, C58, C01–C08).
relationships.display_finding: Error decreased approximately as a power of training-set size before the fixed model reached its plateau.

relationships.condition: Compound-divergence splits (CD 0.1–0.6) and related-domain data mixtures
relationships.reason: High-divergence curves show a slow warm-up then a steeper drop, not a single power law (C09–C56). Domain distance raises plateaus (C58, C60). Adding off-distribution data increases error at 100k target examples (C59). The power-law form depends on train-test distribution.
relationships.display_finding: High-divergence curves warmed up slowly before dropping more steeply, domain distance raised error plateaus, and adding off-distribution data increased error at 100k target examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: U-CFQ compound-divergence splits, tested training sizes and divergence levels
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported curves the paper describes rough power-law behavior over ranges and flattening or continued curvature rather than one unchanging curve; Table 9 and Figure 2 rows C01–C56 document the tested error-rate points.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random splits with rule scope and related-domain training mixtures varied, under the paper's fixed model and training schedule
reader_labels.reason: Curve shape and plateau level depend on rule scope and training-data mixture; higher scope or greater domain distance raises the plateau, and supplementary data can increase errors when target examples are not sufficiently weighted (C57–C60).
